newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria relies on sell-offs to cover bank deposit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria relies on sell-offs to cover bank deposit.

text.p: Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov on Monday said the government relied on privatisation deals worth more than one billion dollars by the year-end to cover citizens' deposits in ailing banks.
In a televised address Videnov said the government has approved the privatisation deals on Sunday. He did not name the state plants, which would be sold.
"Guaranteeing citizens' deposits through privatising big, well-known and competitve Bulgarian enterprises is an effective and hopeful mechanism," Videnov said.
On Monday the central bank (BNB) put under a special supervision nine ailing state and private banks in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector.
The banks are Trade and Savings Bank, Balkanbank, Economic Bank, Businessbank, Elitbank, Slavyani Commercial Bank, Mollov Bank, Yambol Commercial Bank and Dobrudzha Commercial Bank.

Videnov said the government would guarantee the reliability of the state banks which were not affected by the BNB's decision such as Bulbank, United Bulgarian Bank, Post Bank, Hebros, Express and Biohim.
He said the government, together with the BNB and the State Savings Bank, would support the remaining state and private banks.
"We will support all projects related to attracting new considerable investment to the Bulgarian banking system including the banks, placed today under a special supervision," Videnov said.
He warned that the government's restructuring programme could be easily discredited by legal red-tape in bank insolvency cases and urged parliament to speed it up.

"We are convinced that during the second (final) reading of the privatisation law this week the parliament will categorically back the government's acts for reducing the state debt through privatisation deals," Videnov said.
Bulgaria, which has a total foreign debt of 1.186 billion, faces payments worth $680 million to foreign creditors in the second half of this year.
Bulgaria's domestic debt totals some 600 billion levs.
Bulgaria pledged to close down loss-makers including banks by end-September.

Monday's BNB decision on the nine banks followed yet another bid to meet funding reqiurements of international lenders after opening insolvency procedures through the courts against five banks in May and June.
Videnov said he hoped the legal system would also "immediately and adequately respond to the just society demands for severe punishment of financial criminals."
He said the government was ready to submit to parliament this week minor legal changes aimed at strengthening the country's relations with international financial institutions.
Bulgaria's Socialist government hopes to win a delayed second $115 million tranche of funding at the IMF/World Bank annual meeting due in October.
